title: Meager Success: A Theory of the Unlearnable for Hypothesis Testing
summary: When the standard of pointwise consistency for statistical inference -- convergence to the truth in every possible state of the world -- is provably unachievable, the usual responses are to change the inferential target or to strengthen background assumptions. This paper pursues a third: hold the inference problem fixed and identify the highest standard that remains achievable. I define a hierarchy of standards weaker than pointwise consistency, cast in topological terms, requiring convergence to the truth not everywhere but on a ``large'' set of probability measures.
